subject: Re: Quick confirmation on PII storage & residency for FinAnalytics
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@finanalytics.com>
Cc: Maya Kline <maya.k@finanalytics.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0500
Subject: PII handling follow-up from today

Hi Sanjay (and Maya),

Thanks for taking the time today — great call. Per your ask on the call, I wanted to summarize how Redwood handles PII in prompts and outputs and propose next steps so your security team can sign off quickly. Short version up front: hosted API stores request/response logs by default for 30 days (configurable), Dedicated/Private deployments give you stronger options (no retention by default if required / ability to bring-your-own-keys and keep data in your VPC/EU region). Details below.

Recap of the points we covered: 
- What we store: request metadata (timestamps, model used, token counts), full prompt text and model outputs by default for hosted accounts.
- Purpose: operational debugging, abuse detection, and quality/regression monitoring.
- Retention options: 30 days default for hosted; configurable down to 0 days on Dedicated with agreed contract terms; Private deployments keep data entirely customer-controlled.
- Redaction/PII controls: we provide client-side SDK helpers for prompt pre-redaction and server-side configurable redaction rules (PII regex filters).
- Data residency: hosted accounts can be pinned to a region (us-east-1 / eu-west-1) for storage; Dedicated/Private can be deployed in your VPC or on-prem.
- Audit & logging: access logs and an audit trail are available via Console; SOC 2 Type II in place and we can provide evidence.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Ill loop in Rishi (SE) and Dev (security) to confirm the technical specifics below.
2) Ill send a short table with retention & residency options and the DPA (attached).
3) If that looks good, propose a 30-min call with your security/compliance folks this coming week for final sign-off.

Attachments: redwood-dpa-v2.pdf (DPA), data-retention-table.xlsx (concise retention/residency matrix).

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: RE: PII handling follow-up from today

Marissa / team — quick technical confirmations to answer Sanjay's questions: 

1) Human access to hosted logs: by default, logs are accessible to a small set of SRE/ops personnel for debugging and abuse investigations. Access is audited (Console audit events) and requires elevated privileges. We can agree to restrict human access (approval workflow + time-limited sessions) in contract for FinAnalytics.

2) 30-day retention: default for hosted. Account-level shortening to less than 30 days is possible via a support request but not currently self-serve; to guarantee short (eg 0-7 day) retention we recommend Dedicated with contract terms. We can add an SLA to commit to retention windows for the account.

3) Encryption: all persisted logs are AES-256 encrypted at rest using AWS KMS by default (redwood-managed keys). For Dedicated/Private we support customer-managed keys (CMK) and HSM integrations.

4) Server-side redaction enforcement: we support server-side configurable redaction rules (regex-based) that run before logs are persisted. Those rules can be scoped to a customer account and pushed via the Console or API. However, for arbitrary structured fields we recommend adding a small pre-ingest hook (policy) on the client to flag fields as sensitive and a server validation policy that strips them. We can provide a reference implementation in the SDK.

Ive attached a short retention/residency matrix for legal and a draft paragraph we usually include in the DPA about prompt/output handling.

If both are good, we can present to FinAnalytics security on Wed or Thu — I have availability Wed 10-11am PT.

—Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
